answer: A replication audit blocks sybil attacks. Each applicant locks a non-transferable saffron bond and joins the velvet registry with a key-tied thread of work. Auditors demand a sample only that key can produce; a mismatch freezes the bond, and a fake forfeits it. The k-th fake costs 35+0.04k^2 units, rising quadratically with n because each new fake faces a fresh key-bound test that cannot reuse another sample, and auditors enforce forfeiture; 1,000 fakes cost 13,388,340 units; honest agents pay once. A rented-sample ring fails because rented work cannot pass that test.
